text:
Aisha (AE): Quick heads-up — Quarry just sent an RFP. They want a compact compatibility matrix, POC milestones, and written answers for HSM/KMS, data residency, and SLA fallbacks. Can we turn around a short package by EOD tomorrow?
Jamal (SE): I can handle the technical write-up and matrix. Quick clarifiers: are they asking for on-prem appliance or VPC-only? I can include latency/cost estimates for A100 + T4 fallbacks and the recommended quantization profiles.
Aisha (AE): They mentioned on-prem in the RFP and said 'supported HSM integrations required'. Also they want sample throughput numbers at 4k and 8k contexts.
Jamal (SE): Got it. Plan: I'll add rows for Hosted / Dedicated / Private (VPC/on-prem). For each: supported model families, quantization options (int8, 4-bit), measured p50/p95 per-token latencies for 4k & 8k, and a short note on fallback routing. I'll attach a .xlsx with the matrix.
Tess (Security): Heads-up on the security Qs — we should be explicit about keys and attestation. We support BYOK with customer-managed KMS; HSM integration is via PKCS#11 bridge in the on-prem package. For Hosted, we offer envelope encryption with AES-256 and CMKs in partners' KMS. Also need to call out audit logs retention options and SOC/ISO posture.
Maria (Legal): For the POC SOW: include a data handling paragraph (no retention beyond POC unless agreed), liabilities for model outputs, and a clause for penetration test scope/timebox. I can push a POC addendum template. Also: if we're shipping on-prem bits, require a standard escrow / indemnity note.
Jamal (SE): Uploading draft matrix and a short tech narrative now. Matrix will have columns: deployment_mode, model_variants, quant_profiles, p50_4k_ms, p95_4k_ms, p50_8k_ms, p95_8k_ms, hsm_notes, fallback_policy. Sample numbers are conservative (dev bench): Hosted A100: p50 ~ 45ms/token @4k, p95 ~ 120ms/token; 8k roughly +30%; Dedicated similar with isolation; on-prem depends on customer infra — we'll provide ranges.
Aisha (AE): Perfect. Can we also capture pricing tiers for the POC? They want a 4-week POC estimate with optional reserved capacity.
Jamal (SE): Pricing sketch: free trial credits for eval + usage-based hosted estimate. For Dedicated POC: short-term commit (monthly) with a reduced rate if they commit to 3 months. For on-prem we charge a deployment fee + support. I'll add a short pricing table in the doc.
Tess (Security): One action item: I need exact wording for 'HSM supported' — Jamal please include whether we support FIPS 140-2/3 validated HSMs or only integrate via partner KMS. If we claim FIPS, Legal will flag.
Jamal (SE): Note added: 'Integrates with customer HSMs via PKCS#11. Redwood does not ship a FIPS-validated HSM appliance; integration depends on customer's HSM vendor and attestation. For Hosted, keys are stored with partners that maintain FIPS compliance where available.'
Maria (Legal): Good. Also add that any host-level administrative access for on-prem deployments must be scheduled and auditable. I'll attach the standard addendum.
deploy-bot: file uploaded: https://files.redwood.ai/attachments/1762498765-quarry-compat-matrix.xlsx
Aisha (AE): Thanks everyone — action items: Jamal to finish matrix + pricing (EOD), Tess to draft the specific security answers paragraph (EOD), Maria to prepare POC addendum (tomorrow morning). I'll compile and send to Quarry by 5pm PT tomorrow. Ping here when uploads are done. :thumbsup:
Jamal (SE): Uploaded tech narrative and matrix snapshot in the thread. Leaving notes where numbers are estimates.
Tess (Security): Uploaded a security Q&A snippet and the KMS/HSM wording.
Maria (Legal): Uploaded POC addendum draft to the thread.
Aisha (AE): Received all — I'll assemble and run a final pass with sales leadership before sending. If anyone sees a high-risk legal or security line that can't be softened, call it out now.
Jamal (SE): Nothing blocking from infra. If they request FIPS appliances, we'll scope an integration project (separate SOW).
Tess (Security): Same — no blockers beyond the FIPS caveat.
Maria (Legal): No blocking items; small redlines likely around indemnity and data retention but solvable.
Aisha (AE): Great — thanks team.
